title: aiPHeed: food-insecurity risk indicators for CALABARZON (DA Region IV-A)

served_engine.name: aiPHeed-E49-C2 (E48-A1 LightGBM + shrinkage calibration) - PREVIEW
served_engine.why_served: Preview of E48-A1 (E36 inputs + the five trigger proportions) with E49-C2 shrinkage calibration, in a separate local instance; the official system serves E36. Probabilities are calibrated by shrinkage toward the training base rate (E49-C2); driver shares come from the LightGBM before calibration.
served_engine.evidence_status: EXPERIMENTAL / PREVIEW (E49: lowest Brier among eligible calibration arms; gain over raw E48-A1 not significant)

target_definition.label: T1: S1 = H + 2D > tau, HIGH or LOW (the approved Chapter I composite food-stress label)
target_definition.H: SWS Balance Luzon self-rated hunger (%), one regional value for all five provinces (measured)
target_definition.D: province food inflation minus the five-province mean (pp), PSA provincial CPI (measured)
target_definition.tau: median S1 of the published labelled quarters before the origin (trailing median)
target_definition.observable: after the quarter's SWS round is posted and its last CPI month is released (2026-Q3: 14 Oct 2026)
target_definition.is_not: an official or measured food-insecurity prevalence; provincial differences come only from prices

regional_hunger.what: SWS self-rated involuntary hunger, Balance Luzon (Luzon outside Metro Manila)
regional_hunger.geographic_level: regional: ONE value shared by all five provinces; not a provincial or municipal measurement

quarters.status: development backtest: nested walk-forward, refitted at this origin with only information published before it; the outcome had been examined in earlier experiments

lgu_ranking.meaning: Indicative, relative ordering of the 142 cities and municipalities for planning attention. It is the province estimate re-weighted by PSA 2021 poverty incidence (60%) and 2024 POPCEN population density (40%) inside each province. It is not a measured municipal food-insecurity rate, not an independent municipal forecast and not an official classification (Chapter I, 1.7). The province estimate it starts from has NOT been validated against baselines (E25-E28), so the ranking inherits that status: EXPERIMENTAL.
does_not_mean: It does not say that any LGU is food insecure, or how many households are.

Positions inside a province reflect the vulnerability weights only. Positions across provinces are not a measured comparison: the vulnerability index is scaled 0 to 1 inside each province, so the region-wide order mixes five different scales and follows the within-province index more than the province estimate (E35-D4). Compare LGUs within their province.

For an LGU without a PSA municipal poverty estimate (Lucena City, a highly urbanized city that the PSA no-HUC table excludes), the poverty term is a province substitute, so its position inside the province comes from population density and the substitute value, not from a municipal measurement.
Two LGUs with equal risk_index share a rank; their listing order (PSGC) carries no meaning.

lgu_ranking.method: vulnerability = 0.6 x poverty_norm + 0.4 x density_norm (min-max within province); risk_index = province probability x vulnerability, clamp [0,1], 4 dp; competition ranks, ties by PSGC; null probability -> null risk and ranks

threshold_75pct.verdict: One-quarter-ahead accuracy of the proposed LightGBM on 65 development estimates (13 quarters, 2023-Q1 to 2026-Q3): 55/65 = 0.846. The point estimate is above 75%, but the 95% date-bootstrap interval (0.769 to 0.923) reaches below 75%, so the target is not demonstrated. Always-HIGH reaches 0.815 and persistence a higher one (0.877). Unlike always-HIGH, the model does identify LOW quarters (balanced accuracy 0.841). No paired difference with any of the six baselines is significant. These are development dates; the 2026-Q4 forecast is the first untouched test.

next_quarter_evaluation.verdict: Next-quarter accuracy 39/55 = 0.709 (95% date-bootstrap 0.582-0.836): the 75% target is NOT met. Persistence reaches 0.800. No paired difference with the six thesis models is significant. Validation status: NOT DEMONSTRATED.

limitations: The label is dominated by one regional SWS hunger value, so in most quarters all five provinces share a label; 53 of 65 development labels are HIGH. Provincial differences come mainly from relative food prices.

One-quarter-ahead accuracy is 0.846 on 65 development estimates, above always-HIGH (0.815) and below persistence (0.877). The 75% target is met as a point estimate but not demonstrated (95% interval reaches 0.769). No baseline is beaten significantly.
News signals added no measurable skill: the government-only LightGBM (B5) scores as well or better than the combined model on the same rows.
News evidence is title-only (Google News RSS), thin in older quarters, and its relevance labels were made by the AI assistant; a researcher re-review is pending.

LGU rankings re-weight the province forecast by PSA 2021 municipal poverty (141 of 142 LGUs; Lucena City, a highly urbanized city absent from the PSA no-HUC table, uses a province substitute of unverified source) and 2024 POPCEN density. They are relative positions, not municipal forecasts.
The next-quarter forecast (two quarters after the latest complete data quarter) scored 39/55 = 0.709 on development dates (E38), below 75%; persistence scored 0.800. Reliability is not established.
The 2026-Q4 and 2027-Q1 forecasts are the first untouched tests; they can be scored only after the SWS December 2026 and March 2027 rounds are released.
